name: Heavy Favourite Holder
rule: On an active universe market with volume >= 10,000 contracts, buy the side whose ask is between 0.85 and 0.97 and whose displayed spread is <= 4c, sizing 25% of cash, and hold to the official settlement.
why: Favourite-longshot bias: the over-bought side is the longshot, so heavy favourites are (if the bias exists) slightly under-priced and pay a small, repeatable edge at settlement. No exit logic: the trade is the settlement.
failure_mode: Every settled upset costs nearly the whole stake; a run of upsets erases many wins. Fees on high-volume favourites are also the largest in absolute dollars.

evidence.claim: Favourite-longshot bias is documented across parimutuel and prediction markets; a CEPR/VoxEU column analyses 300k+ Kalshi contracts specifically.
Kalshi quadratic taker fee 0.07*C*P*(1-P) applied to every fill in the ledger.

name: Longshot Fader
rule: On an active universe market with 24h volume >= 5,000, when the cheap side's ask is between 0.03 and 0.15 and the opposite side's ask is between 0.85 and 0.97 with displayed spread <= 5c, buy the opposite (85-97c) side, sizing 25% of cash, and hold to settlement.
why: Same bias viewed from the longshot side: when a market is quoting 3-15c for the underdog, the favourite is the side the bias says is cheap. Entering from the longshot quote makes the trigger observable without estimating anything.
failure_mode: Identical to SurePenny: upsets are near-total losses. Extra risk: thin 24h volume can mean the 3-15c quote is stale, so the fill may be worse than the displayed ask.

evidence.claim: Same CEPR/VoxEU favourite-longshot analysis as SurePenny.

name: Expiry Convergence
rule: Inside 24 hours of expected_expiration_time (or close_time when no expected time is published), buy any side whose ask is between 0.90 and 0.99 on a universe market with volume >= 1,000, sizing 20% of cash, and hold to the official settlement.
why: In the final hours the remaining uncertainty is small and the 90-99c side is usually right; convergence trades pay 1-10c per contract with a high hit rate. Return-seeking: capital is kept working rather than parked.
failure_mode: One 2% probability upset per trade destroys ~50 winners at this stake. Settlement rules disputes (can_close_early, rules_primary wording) are the tail risk; the ledger records rules_primary with every entry.

evidence.claim: Rule is a documented convergence hypothesis; the independent test is the forward ledger itself (verified fills and official settlements only).

name: 24h Momentum Rider
rule: When the market's official previous_price_dollars exists, the market is >= 24h old, and |last - previous| >= 0.03, buy the direction of the move at its ask with a +2c limit, sizing 15% of cash. Exit: sell when the bid is >= entry + 5c, else hold to settlement.
why: Short-horizon momentum: a 3c+ one-day move on an event contract often reflects information that is still being priced. Both the signal (previous_price_dollars) and the dates come from the official market object.
failure_mode: The previous_price field is the previous day's close, which can be stale on thin markets; fills are book-dependent so a stale signal plus a thin book is the worst case. The 5c target rarely hits, so most trades ride to settlement.

evidence.claim: Momentum is a tested anomaly family in equity and futures markets; transfer to event contracts is UNVERIFIED and the forward ledger is the test.

name: 10c Mean Reversion
rule: When |last - previous| >= 0.10: if last <= previous - 0.10 and last <= 0.45, buy YES at its ask (limit ask + 2c); if last >= previous + 0.10 and last >= 0.55, buy NO at its ask. Size 15% of cash. Exit at 2x entry if the bid reaches it, else hold to settlement.
why: Large one-day moves on binary contracts can overshoot: paying <= 45c for a side that 'dropped' 10c is betting the move exaggerated. The 2x target caps the winner size; settlement is the default exit.
failure_mode: If the move is news (a real regime change), the fade keeps losing: adverse selection is the whole story. The backtest on verified candles decides whether this rule even earns a forward slot.

evidence.claim: Mean reversion vs momentum in short-horizon binaries is an open question for event contracts; treated as a hypothesis to be tested on this data, not assumed.

name: Crossed-Book Hunter
rule: If the derived quotes satisfy YES ask + NO ask <= 0.99 (buying both sides costs under $1.00), buy equal quantities of both sides (size: the larger affordable side at 10% of cash). Both legs pay exactly $1.00 at settlement, so the gross capture is (1.00 - total cost) per pair minus both taker fees.
why: A strict, self-verifying arbitrage: no forecast, no model, just two displayed asks that cannot both be fair. In a consistent reciprocal book this condition should never hold — so the rule doubles as a book-consistency monitor: if it never triggers, that is itself a verified observation.
failure_mode: Leg risk: if the NO ask quote disappears between reading the book and the simulated fill, the strategy logs a BLOCKED intent instead of guessing. Fees can eat a 1-2c capture, which the ledger shows per trade.

evidence.claim: Reciprocal quoting (YES ask = 1 - NO bid) is the exchange's own documented structure; a crossing condition is a direct arithmetic consequence of it.

name: Depth Imbalance Diver
rule: On a universe market with displayed bid depth on BOTH sides, compute imbalance = (YES depth - NO depth) / (YES depth + NO depth). If |imbalance| >= 0.40, buy the heavier side at its ask (limit ask + 2c), sizing 15% of cash, and hold to settlement.
why: Visible resting liquidity is a cheap public signal: persistent one-sided depth can reflect informed flow or stale quotes. The rule logs the full level list with every fill so the claim can be audited bar by bar.
failure_mode: Displayed depth can be pulled (stale quotes) or is genuinely uninformative; imbalance can also mean the heavy side is about to be hit through. The forward ledger is the test — similarity to order-flow imbalance in equity microstructure is explicitly NOT assumed to transfer.

evidence.claim: Order-book imbalance is a documented short-horizon signal in equity microstructure literature; transfer to prediction markets is UNVERIFIED here.

name: Penny Longshot Lottery
rule: On a universe market with traded volume, buy any side whose ask is between 0.01 and 0.05, sizing 10% of cash. Exit when the bid is >= 2x entry, else hold to the official settlement.
why: Deliberate max-return construction: pay pennies, and a win pays 100-200x. If the market over-prices longshots (the same bias SurePenny trades from the other side), the pennies are cheap; if the bias is absent, this is the strategy that bleeds — and the ledger will show exactly that.
failure_mode: Most tickets settle at zero; exits are rare because one-sided books keep the bid at 0.00, so the 2x target usually never prints. Expect the worst equity curve in the race.

evidence.claim: Lottery demand for longshots is documented in prediction markets (demand for low-probability outcomes); treated here as a hypothesis, sized down, and tracked separately.

name: Macro Expiry Closer
rule: On official macro series (KXCPI, KXFED, KXU6, KXNFP — final universe tickers listed in data/universe.json), inside 6 hours of close_time, buy the side whose ask is between 0.80 and 0.97 with displayed spread <= 3c, sizing 25% of cash, and hold to settlement.
why: Macro binary markets converge fast near release time: once the print is out or the range is nearly certain, the heavy side is cheap relative to its true probability. Small edge, very high hit rate, capital always working.
failure_mode: Macro upsets are fat-tailed exactly when they matter (surprise prints); a single 90c loss costs ~10 wins. The rules_primary text (which exact print/threshold settles the market) is logged on every entry because rule wording IS the risk.

evidence.claim: The convergence pattern is observed in the committed candle archive (data/candles/) for KXCPI/KXFED markets; the forward ledger is the independent test.

name: Commodity Directional Drift
rule: On the official daily commodity/crypto direction markets in the universe (e.g. KXWTI, KXBTC, KXGOLD, KXETH — final tickers in data/universe.json), when the market's own last price implies a >= 0.70 probability for one direction and it is inside 12 hours of settlement, buy that side at ask (limit ask + 2c), sizing 20% of cash, hold to settlement.
why: Daily price-direction binaries on established commodities embed the spot-vs-strike gap; in the final 12h the gap usually holds, so the 70-97c side should be slightly cheap. This is the cross-market bridge: the 'signal' is the market's own pricing of a physical commodity, which can be cross-checked against official commodity data (see research DB).
failure_mode: Commodity gaps over the settlement window (overnight moves, exchange close rules) break the 70c+ side. Settlement uses the official source named in the market's rules; if that source's final print differs from the live spot, the trade loses regardless of the model.

evidence.claim: The spot-vs-strike relationship is checked against the official settlement source named in each market's rules_primary; the forward ledger is the test.
